headline: Highest risk is data leakage: ms-swift can read/write files and call external APIs, while dagster is a non-runnable orchestrator with no filesystem or network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, filesystem, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest ms-swift output by default. ms-swift can emit text via stdin/stdout and operate on files, but the pair lacks a documented shared bridge. Any injection would require unusual manual transfer or external orchestration.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies ms-swift output into dagster task definitions or config files, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF an external shared filesystem or message queue is introduced, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep outputs out of task specs and config files.
Use a strict text-only review step before any manual transfer.
Disable any shared clipboard or paste automation.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, but ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets and can read/write files plus call allowlisted APIs. If both are pointed at the same workspace, ms-swift can expose sensitive artifacts through its outputs or uploads. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace containing datasets, checkpoints, or logs, leakage becomes plausible.
IF ms-swift is configured to upload artifacts or logs to external services, exposure increases.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent.
Restrict ms-swift to non-sensitive sample data.
Rotate or remove hub_token and sdk-token before runs.
Review upload destinations in ms-swift configs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git state, or use the network, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with ms-swift in the documented default profile. ms-swift can write files and spawn subprocesses, but without a shared writable target or locking primitive, the overlap is limited and not a default conflict.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locks, conflict risk rises.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared configs.
Serialize any file-producing steps.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is an orchestrator, so if it consumes ms-swift-generated artifacts or summaries as pipeline inputs, it may treat them as authoritative. ms-swift can produce logs, evaluation outputs, and configuration data, creating a plausible chain where unchecked outputs propagate into downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented roles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF dagster pipelines ingest ms-swift outputs without validation, errors can cascade downstream.
IF ms-swift-generated configs are auto-applied, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Add schema validation before ingestion.
Require human review for generated configs.
Compare outputs against a known-good baseline.
Log and quarantine unexpected artifacts.
requires-engineering: implement signed artifact verification.

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift handles hub_token and sdk-token and touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and training outputs, while dagster is a data-orchestration tool with no declared sensitive-data handling. If regulated data is routed through ms-swift, retention and residency obligations can diverge from dagster-managed workflows. Dagster is not cited for a specific residency claim because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated datasets or secrets are processed through ms-swift, retention and access controls must be checked.
IF dagster stores pipeline metadata longer than the source system allows, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to ms-swift.
Remove secrets from logs and checkpoints.
Set explicit retention windows for artifacts.
Confirm residency and DPA terms for any external uploads.
requires-engineering: align lifecycle policies across both systems.
